fact_card.purpose: Emphasise one to three consequential facts the narration has just told.
fact_card.schema_text: {"facts": [{"text": "a short sentence of at most 90 characters, in the narration's own words", "fact_id": "unit key of the sentence it comes from"}]} - one to three facts.

facts.text: Officers found two spent casings by the bed.

recap.purpose: Orient the viewer: what is confirmed, what is disputed, what is still unknown, each as a few key words.
recap.schema_text: {"confirmed": [{"text": "at most 38 characters", "fact_id": "unit key"}] (up to 3), "disputed": [same] (up to 2), "unknown": [same] (up to 2)} - only the sections that have items; every text at most 38 characters.

conflict.purpose: Isolate one real disagreement between two accounts the narration has told.
conflict.schema_text: {"conflict": {"id": "c1", "title": "the point in dispute, at most 70 characters", "kind": "parties|witnesses|evidence", "status": "open", "summary": "at most 60 characters"}, "sides": [{"who": "who says it", "claim": "what they say, at most 160 characters", "source": "where it was said (statement, testimony, report)", "fact_id": "unit key"}, {the second side}]} - exactly two sides that really contradict each other.

conflict.title: Was the garage door open?
conflict.summary: Two accounts of the same door

evidence_check.purpose: Explain what one piece of evidence establishes, what it does not, and how the jury or the record treated it.
evidence_check.schema_text: {"item": {"name": "at most 48 characters", "fact_id": "unit key"}, "establishes": [{"text": "at most 90 characters", "basis": "fact", "fact_id": "unit key"}] (1-2), "not_establishes": [same] (0-2), "supported_by": [same] (0-2), "contradicted_by": [same] (0-2), "assessment": {"text": "at most 90 characters", "basis": "finding", "fact_id": "unit key"}} - basis is one of fact, allegation, witness, expert, finding, disputed; no percentages or scores.

establishes.text: He wrote of wanting her dead.

not_establishes.text: They do not show who fired.

assessment.text: The jury treated them as central.

forensic.purpose: Explain one forensic examination: the sample, how the method works, the reported result and its limits.
forensic.schema_text: {"exam": "dna|fingerprint|toxicology|trace|fiber_hair|digital|ballistics|bloodstain", "sample": {"text": "at most 90 characters", "basis": "fact|finding|expert", "fact_id": "unit key"}, "method": {"text": "a plain general description of the method, at most 110 characters", "basis": "illustration"}, "result": {"text": "at most 110 characters", "basis": "fact|finding|expert|allegation", "fact_id": "unit key"}, "limits": {"text": "at most 110 characters", "basis": "fact|finding|expert|unknown", "fact_id": "unit key"}} - limits may be left out; the method is the one item with no fact_id.

method.text: Marks on a casing are compared with test shots.

result.text: Both casings came from one 9mm gun.

limits.text: No firearm was recovered to compare.
